general_information.Description: Drawing subject illustrates the basic content of the painting to give students the general concept for further studying of ratio, morphology, shape, characteristics, state of people and objects in relation to space and environment by dark-bright contrasts. Through the process of research, students will grasp the basic principles of descriptive geometry while enhancing the aesthetic awareness. Drawing is the knowledge basement for students to understand the structure, proportions, shapes to serve the art works. In the process of practice and studies descriptive geometry, students shall gain a wealth of knowledge and resources to support artistic creation. Drawing helps students understand the aesthetic standards and enhance the aesthetic emotions, which is the basis for artistic creativity. -The subject will be carried out in the drawing studio with specific requirements on learning materials. -Students familiarize themselves with drawing tools and correct pencil holding style, the notions of color, shadows, dark shadow, reflection, etc. and with the basic fragment and hatch techniques in drawing. Then, students study methods of rendering, theory of light and materials through the study of the basic shapes: spherical shape, cubic shape, etc. .. Students will find plenty of helpful tips on choosing the right tools and materials, fundamental drawing techniques,developing value and shading, and setting up an effective composition, as well as important information about the influences of perspective, balance, and texture. Detailed examples of animals, people, flowers the still-life and landscapes will help guide learners through the most challenging aspects of drawing almost anything, from basic shapes to realistic details. The subject will be deployed in the studio with all requirements for learning tools for the subject.
general_information.StudentTasks: 1. Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend at least 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination 2. Actively participate in class activities 3. Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class 4. Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose 5. Read the textbook in advance 6. Access the course website (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course. 7. Complete course's Portfolio with full contents of exercises and submit to the teacher the week before the end of the course.
general_information.Tools: Individual tools prepared by students: - Paper (size A3). Sketching papper sheet (A3) - Color, pencil, eraser, brushes, back ink pen, artlines, markers - Paper knife, roll of paper tape, - Laptop - Drawing boad

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Understand what the drawing is and seeing thing through basic shapes.
Use drawing tools effectively. Use the ways that measure objects. Create the illusion of three dimensions in a two-dimensional space with perspective to develope form.
Analyze the relation between objects and light sources. Define hightlights, shadow areas, cast shadows and reflected light.
Organize layout for a drawing and create sketch by using lines with value. Use the ways to make fragmentation and hatch while sketch.
Perform the unique properties of objects. Transfer the color of objects into monochrome drawing.
Have a professional style in design activities_drawing forms and still-life. Shows patience, concentration, and diligence throughout the course

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Learners are able to understand materials and apply pencil material techniques to express shapes and spaces in black and white on A3 paper.
assessments.Grading Guide: LAB 1, LAB 2 (practice 1): DRAWING BASIC BLOCKS Lab 1: Practice drawing cubes + Lab 2: Practice drawing basic blocks. With the guidance of the lecturer. Students do the hand drawing and submit the results to the lecturer in class. The practice score can be announced to students at the end of the lesson. The lecturer evaluates and scores the students' drawings. Arrange the shapes in the paper frame, clearly balance the main and secondary. The size ratio between the blocks and compared to the paper size. Draw basic blocks in space (circle, cylinder, box, sphere...) Describe the light and dark, block and light. How to use lines to describe shapes , Completeness: complete, clean,

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Learners are able to understand the materials and apply pencil material techniques to express shapes and spaces in black and white on paper. A3,Overview of basic blocks, measuring and plumb methods, construction methods in drawings of these blocks
assessments.Grading Guide: LAB 3, LAB 4 (practice 1): DRAWING A SET OF OBJECTS Lab 3: Practice drawing a set of still life with basic objects arranged by the teacher. Lab 4: Students practice drawing still life with objects of difficult shapes With the guidance of the lecturer. Students do the drawing by hand and submit the results to the lecturer in class. The practice score can be announced to students at the end of the lesson. The lecturer evaluates and scores the students' drawings. Choose a layout on paper. Arrange the images in the paper frame, clearly balancing the main and secondary. The drawing has the correct proportions between objects (height, width, size), clearly showing the shape of the sample object in space. Expresses the correlation between light and dark, large light and dark interface. The use of lines to describe objects is solid and coherent . The drawing is complete with space, depth, and cleanliness.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Learners are able to understand materials and apply pencil techniques to represent shapes and spaces in black and white on A3 paper, an overview of basic deformed blocks, objects and fruits, measuring and plumb methods, and methods of constructing shapes in drawings of these blocks;
assessments.Grading Guide: PRACTICE 5, PRACTICE 6 (practice 1): DRAW A STILL LIFE PRACTICE 5: Students observe the set of still life paintings introduced by the teacher in class, inspired by the still life paintings, imagine and compose a still life painting with animals. PRACTICE 6: Students observe the set of still life paintings prepared by the teacher in class Choose a composition on paper. Arrange the images in the paper frame harmoniously, clearly balanced between the main and secondary. The painting has the correct structure of the object, relative proportions, shape of the sample object and compare with the size of the paper. Express the shape of the object in space Accurately determine the light source, clear light - dark areas. Clearly divide light and dark. Creates depth, space and atmosphere for the entire painting. The painting is solid, coherent, and has highlights (bold/light lines). The painting is sharp, depicting the beauty of the subject. The painting is complete, with enough space, depth and clarity.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Master principles of composition, proportion, form, light, and shadow. Develop ideas from real-life observation for creative artworks. Select, arrange, and transform still life objects into a harmonious, lively composition. Express lines, values, and colors effectively, emphasizing the focal point. Strengthen skills of observation, analysis, and synthesis for creative composition.
assessments.Grading Guide: LAB 7, LAB 8 (practice 1): DRAWING A STILL LIFE ART WORK LAB 7: Students observe a set of still life paintings presented by the teacher in class, inspired by the still life paintings, imagine and create a still life art work with animals. (Version 1), LAB 8: Students observe a set of still life paintings prepared by the teacher in class (Version 2 can draw lines and doodles) Balanced, harmonious arrangement within the paper frame; objects connected, with clear focus; avoid emptiness or overcrowding. Correct structure, proportion, and spatial form; no distortion or imbalance. Clear light source; smooth transitions; depth and atmosphere created. Solid, coherent, with accents; avoid smudges; lines express object quality. Clean, complete work with space and depth; conveys artistic feeling.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Understand the difference between still life creation and drawing from models; master composition, proportion, form, light, and shadow. Develop creative ideas from real-life observation. Select, arrange, and transform objects into a harmonious, dynamic composition. Apply lines, values, and colors expressively, emphasizing the focal point. Practice observation, analysis, and synthesis; create a still life painting with creativity, personal style, and sound artistic principles.
assessments.Grading Guide: LAB 9, LAB 10 (practice 5): Create a still life with a mask Lab 9: Students observe a set of still life paintings presented by the teacher in class, get inspired by the still life paintings, imagine and create a still life artwork with a mask (Version 1) Lab 10: Students observe a set of still life paintings prepared by the teacher in class, get inspired by the still life paintings, imagine and create a still life artwork with a mask (Version 2) Balanced layout, clear focal point, proper spacing. Accurate structure and proportion, solid forms in space, no distortion. Clear light source, smooth tonal transitions, depth and atmosphere. Confident, clear, with variation in weight; neat and expressive of texture. Clean, spatial, expressive, showing personal aesthetics. (+ bonus for creativity and visual appeal). After finishing the drawing by hand, students may use AI to add simple animation for enhanced presentation.
Participation grade will be given based on students' attendance, students' attitude, preparation, contribution of discussions.
